metadata.title: [FIX][RBAC]: Check team-scoped permissions in AdminAuthMiddleware for team-scoped requests
metadata.author: madhav165

description:
# 🐛 Bug-fix PR
Fixes #3380

---

## 📌 Summary
`has_admin_permission()` in `AdminAuthMiddleware` only checked global/personal roles when determining admin UI access. Users with team-scoped roles (`developer`, `viewer`) that include `admin.dashboard` were denied access with 403 when accessing `/admin?team_id=...`, even though they should be able to view the dashboard within their team scope.

## 🔁 Reproduction Steps
1. Create a user with only a team-scoped `developer` role (no global `platform_viewer`)
2. Access `/admin?team_id=<valid_team_id>` with that user's session JWT
3. Observe 403 redirect to login page
4. Server log: `"Admin access denied for user without admin permissions: <email>"`

## 🐞 Root Cause
`has_admin_permission()` (`permission_service.py:163`) called `get_user_permissions(user_email)` with no `team_id`, causing `_get_user_roles()` to return only global + personal roles. Team-scoped roles with `admin.dashboard` were invisible to the check.

The `AdminAuthMiddleware` (`main.py:1826`) never extracted or passed the `team_id` from the request query params.

## 💡 Fix Description
- **`AdminAuthMiddleware.dispatch()`**: Extract `team_id` from request query params, validate it against the DB-resolved `token_teams` (already computed earlier in the method), and pass the validated team_id to `has_admin_permission()`.
- **`has_admin_permission()`**: Accept optional `team_id` parameter and forward it to `get_user_permissions()` so team-scoped roles are included.
- Security: `team_id` is validated against server-side DB-resolved teams before use — no privilege escalation possible.

## 🧪 Verification

| Check                                 | Command              | Status |
|---------------------------------------|----------------------|--------|
| Unit tests                            | `uv run pytest`      | ✅     |
| Coverage on changed lines             | `--cov-report`       | ✅ 99% |
| Manual regression no longer fails     | see root cause trace | ✅     |

## ✅ Checklist
- [x] No secrets/credentials committed
- [x] Tests added for new behavior (5 new test cases)
- [x] Backward compatible (team_id defaults to None, preserving existing behavior)

reviews.author: crivetimihai
reviews.body:
## Review Summary

### Security — PASS
- **Privilege escalation**: `validated_team_id` only forwards `team_id` when it is non-empty and present in DB-resolved `token_teams`. All edge cases verified (empty string, admin bypass `None`, invalid team, repeated query keys).
- **Two-layer model preserved**: Layer 1 (token scoping) still rejects public-only tokens before admin checks. Layer 2 (RBAC) still gates admin route entry via `has_admin_permission()`.
- **Input trust**: Raw query `team_id` is never used directly — only `validated_team_id` reaches the permission lookup, and SQL is parameterized via SQLAlchemy.

### Logic — PASS
- `_get_user_roles()` correctly includes global/personal roles plus team-specific + `scope_id IS NULL` roles when `team_id` is set.
- `has_admin_permission()` still short-circuits on DB admin flag, preserves wildcard/`admin.*` checks.
- Backward compatible: `team_id` defaults to `None`, preserving original behavior for all existing call paths.

### Consistency — PASS
- RBAC middleware uses `request.state.team_id` (API routes); AdminAuthMiddleware uses `query_params` (admin UI) — correct for their contexts.
- Same token-team normalization sources (`_resolve_teams_from_db`/`normalize_token_teams`).

### Performance — PASS
- No new DB queries. In-memory `in` check on small team list. Existing permission cache still used.

### Test Coverage — PASS
- 8 total tests covering the feature (5 from PR author + 3 edge-case tests added):
  - Valid team_id grants access
  - Invalid team_id falls back to global check (403)
  - No team_id = original behavior
  - Empty string team_id treated as absent
  - Admin bypass (`token_teams=None`) ignores query team_id
  - Repeated team_id query keys resolved correctly
  - Permission service forwards team_id
  - Permission service defaults to `None`
- All 356 tests pass. 100% differential coverage on new production lines.

commits.message:
fix(rbac): check team-scoped permissions in AdminAuthMiddleware for team-scoped requests

has_admin_permission() only checked global/personal roles, ignoring team-scoped
roles like developer/viewer that include admin.dashboard. When users access the
admin UI with ?team_id=..., the middleware now validates the team_id against
DB-resolved token_teams and passes it to has_admin_permission() for team-scoped
permission evaluation.

Signed-off-by: Madhav Kandukuri <madhav165@gmail.com>
commits.author: Madhav Kandukuri

commits.message:
test(rbac): add edge-case tests for AdminAuthMiddleware team_id validation

Cover three additional edge cases in the team-scoped admin permission check:
- Empty string team_id in query params treated as absent
- Admin bypass (token_teams=None) ignores query team_id
- Repeated team_id query keys resolved via Starlette QueryParams.get()

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
commits.author: Mihai Criveti

commits.message:
fix(rbac): normalize team_id UUID format in AdminAuthMiddleware

Canonicalize query-param team_id to hex before comparing against
DB-resolved token_teams, so hyphenated UUIDs (e.g. from bookmarks or
external clients) match the hex format stored in the database.
Without this, a valid team member using a hyphenated UUID would be
incorrectly denied team-scoped admin access.

Update all team-scoped middleware tests to use valid UUID hex strings
and add regression tests for hyphenated UUID normalization and garbage
team_id rejection.

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
commits.author: Mihai Criveti

commits.message:
fix(rbac): preserve non-UUID team_id for legacy token compatibility

UUID normalization must fall back to the raw value instead of discarding
non-UUID team IDs, so that legacy/CLI tokens with non-UUID team strings
in their claims can still match during the membership check.

Add regression test for non-UUID team_id matching legacy token_teams.

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
